cohorts.name: Iron Deficiency Pattern
cohorts.description: Depleted iron stores with a compensatory rise in iron-binding capacity, with or without established microcytic anaemia.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: Red cell indices come from Blood Counts while iron studies come from Anemia Studies; coeliac serology and faecal occult blood are admitted as supporting signals because they identify the two commonest causes of unexplained iron loss in adults.

triggers.label: Ferritin below 30 ng/mL - depleted iron stores

supporting.label: TIBC raised - compensatory increase in iron-binding capacity
RDW raised - anisocytosis typical of evolving iron deficiency
Reactive thrombocytosis, a recognised accompaniment of iron deficiency
Anti-tTG IgA raised - possible coeliac disease as the underlying cause
Faecal occult blood positive - possible gastrointestinal blood loss

evidence.citation: Camaschella C, N Engl J Med 2015;372:1832-43
evidence.note: Ferritin <30 ng/mL with low transferrin saturation as the most specific pattern for iron deficiency.

evidence.citation: WHO, Serum ferritin concentrations for the assessment of iron status, 2020
evidence.note: Ferritin thresholds for depleted iron stores, noting ferritin's behaviour as an acute-phase reactant.

evidence.citation: Ko CW et al., AGA Clinical Practice Guideline on Gastrointestinal Evaluation of Iron Deficiency Anemia, Gastroenterology 2020;159:1085-94
evidence.note: Coeliac serology and evaluation for gastrointestinal blood loss in unexplained iron deficiency.

diseases.name: Iron Deficiency Anemia
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low Ferritin with Low Iron and elevated TIBC/UIBC'; Related Markers/Tests: Iron, TIBC, UIBC, Ferritin, Transferrin Saturation

diseases.name: Celiac Disease
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated tTG-IgA with compatible symptoms or unexplained iron/folate deficiency'

diseases.name: Malabsorption Syndrome
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests lists Iron studies among the malabsorption marker set

diseases.name: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (Crohn's Disease/Ulcerative Colitis)
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests lists 'Stool analysis (occult blood), CBC' - chronic blood loss from bowel inflammation

cohorts.name: Microcytosis Without Iron Deficiency
cohorts.description: Small red cells with preserved iron stores and a red cell count that is normal or high - the classic screening pattern for a thalassaemia trait rather than iron deficiency.

triggers.label: Ferritin preserved - iron deficiency does not explain the microcytosis
HbA2 at or above 4% - consistent with beta-thalassaemia trait

supporting.label: Red cell count normal or raised despite microcytosis
RDW not raised - favours a trait over evolving iron deficiency

evidence.citation: Origa R, Genet Med 2017;19:609-19
evidence.note: Beta-thalassaemia trait: microcytosis disproportionate to the degree of anaemia, with raised HbA2.

evidence.citation: Mentzer WC, Lancet 1973;1:882
evidence.note: MCV/RBC discrimination between thalassaemia trait and iron deficiency.

evidence.citation: Brancaleoni V et al., Int J Lab Hematol 2016;38(S1):32-40
evidence.note: Laboratory approach to differentiating microcytic anaemias.

diseases.name: Thalassemia (Trait/Major)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Microcytic anemia (low MCV) that doesn't fully correct with iron, especially with a relevant family/ethnic background'; Related Markers/Tests: Hemoglobin, RBC indices, Hemoglobin electrophoresis

diseases.name: Hemoglobin C/E Disease (HbC/HbE)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Mild microcytic anemia with an abnormal hemoglobin fraction on electrophoresis not explained by iron deficiency or thalassemia alone'

diseases.name: Iron Deficiency Anemia
diseases.dm_basis: Listed as the differential this cohort is specifically designed to exclude, via the preserved ferritin criterion

cohorts.name: Macrocytic / Megaloblastic Pattern
cohorts.description: Enlarged red cells with a low B12 and/or folate - the reversible nutritional causes of macrocytic anaemia.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: The clinical reference rows for B12 and folate deficiency both name 'macrocytic anemia on CBC' in their High-Risk Indicators, which requires Blood Counts and Vitamin Profile parameters to be evaluated together.

triggers.label: Vitamin B12 in the deficient range

supporting.label: Homocysteine raised - functional marker of B12/folate status

evidence.citation: Stabler SP, N Engl J Med 2013;368:149-60
evidence.note: Vitamin B12 deficiency: thresholds, macrocytosis and the role of homocysteine as a functional marker.

evidence.citation: Devalia V et al., BCSH Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Cobalamin and Folate Disorders, Br J Haematol 2014;166:496-513
evidence.note: Diagnostic thresholds for B12 and folate and the indeterminate zone.

diseases.name: Vitamin B12 Deficiency
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Vitamin B12 level in the deficient range with macrocytic anemia on CBC'; Related Markers/Tests: Vitamin B12

diseases.name: Folate (B9) Deficiency
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low folate with macrocytic anemia on CBC'; Related Markers/Tests: Vitamin B9 (Folate)

diseases.name: Peripheral Neuropathy
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low B12 or poorly controlled diabetes together with sensory symptoms in a stocking-glove pattern'; Related Markers/Tests: Vitamin B12

diseases.name: Malabsorption Syndrome
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests lists 'Vitamin D/B12/Folate' among the malabsorption marker set

diseases.name: Myelodysplastic Syndrome
diseases.dm_basis: Differential Diagnoses on the MDS row - macrocytosis without a nutritional cause requires haematology review

cohorts.name: Pancytopenia
cohorts.description: Reduction across all three cell lines at once. A pattern that always requires haematology assessment.

supporting.label: Macrocytosis - can accompany marrow failure states

evidence.citation: Killick SB et al., BCSH Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Adult Aplastic Anaemia, Br J Haematol 2016;172:187-207
evidence.note: Pancytopenia definition and the mandatory diagnostic workup including marrow examination.

evidence.citation: Arber DA et al., Blood 2016;127:2391-405
evidence.note: WHO classification: cytopenias as the presenting feature of myelodysplastic syndromes and acute leukaemia.

diseases.name: Aplastic Anemia
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Simultaneous low hemoglobin, low white cell count, and low platelet count (pancytopenia) without an obvious alternate cause'; Related Markers/Tests: Hemoglobin, WBC count, Platelet Count

diseases.name: Myelodysplastic Syndrome
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Persistent unexplained low blood counts (one or more cell lines) not attributable to another cause'

diseases.name: Leukemia (Suspected/Screening)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Markedly abnormal WBC count (very high or low) with abnormal differential, especially with low hemoglobin and platelets together'

diseases.name: Multiple Myeloma
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators reference anaemia as part of the CRAB pattern

cohorts.name: Markedly Abnormal White Cell Pattern
cohorts.description: White cell count very high or very low with an abnormal differential - a screening signal that needs a blood film and haematology review rather than reassurance.

evidence.citation: Arber DA et al., Blood 2016;127:2391-405
evidence.note: WHO classification of myeloid and lymphoid neoplasms; peripheral counts as the initial trigger for marrow evaluation.

evidence.citation: George TI, Hematology Am Soc Hematol Educ Program 2012;2012:475-84
evidence.note: Diagnostic approach to leukocytosis and leukopenia.

diseases.name: Leukemia (Suspected/Screening)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Markedly abnormal WBC count (very high or low) with abnormal differential, especially with low hemoglobin and platelets together'; Severity/Urgency: 'Emergency-level urgency if acute leukemia is suspected'

diseases.name: Lymphoma (Suspected/Screening)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Persistent unexplained lymphadenopathy with elevated LDH and systemic symptoms'; Related Markers/Tests: CBC, LDH

diseases.name: Myelodysplastic Syndrome
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Persistent unexplained low blood counts (one or more cell lines)'

diseases.name: Reactive Leukocytosis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated WBC with a clear infectious/inflammatory trigger and normal differential pattern' - the benign alternative that must be excluded

cohorts.name: Raised Red Cell Mass
cohorts.description: Haemoglobin and haematocrit persistently above range, which may be primary or secondary to hypoxia or dehydration.

supporting.label: Platelets also raised - can accompany a myeloproliferative process

evidence.citation: Arber DA et al., Blood 2016;127:2391-405
evidence.note: WHO haemoglobin/haematocrit thresholds used as the entry criterion for polycythaemia vera evaluation.

evidence.citation: McMullin MF et al., Br J Haematol 2019;184:176-91
evidence.note: Diagnostic approach to erythrocytosis, distinguishing primary from secondary causes.

diseases.name: Polycythemia
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Persistently elevated hemoglobin/hematocrit above normal range'; Related Markers/Tests: RBC count, Hemoglobin, Hematocrit

cohorts.redundancy_note: Haemoglobin, haematocrit and RBC count are three views of one measurement (red cell mass) and share a redundancy group, so requiring two of them made the cluster discount its own second trigger. The reference criterion - 'persistently elevated haemoglobin/hematocrit above normal range' - is met by either, so one is required and agreement between them raises confidence.

cohorts.name: Thrombocytopenia
cohorts.description: Platelet count below range. Severity determines bleeding risk and how urgently it needs attention.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: Dengue serology (Infectious Diseases) and coagulation markers (Blood Clotting) are admitted as supporting signals because the clinical reference Dengue Fever and DIC rows both hinge on a falling platelet count.

supporting.label: Rising haematocrit - plasma leakage pattern in dengue
Mean platelet volume raised - suggests peripheral destruction rather than reduced marrow production

evidence.citation: Neunert C et al., American Society of Hematology 2019 Guidelines for Immune Thrombocytopenia, Blood Adv 2019;3:3829-66
evidence.note: Platelet thresholds and the diagnosis of ITP by exclusion.

evidence.citation: WHO, Dengue Guidelines for Diagnosis, Treatment, Prevention and Control, 2009
evidence.note: Falling platelet count with rising haematocrit as a warning sign in dengue.

diseases.name: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Markedly low platelet count with bleeding symptoms'; Related Markers/Tests: Platelet count

diseases.name: Dengue Fever
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive NS1/IgM with falling platelet count and rising hematocrit'; Related Markers/Tests: Dengue NS1 antigen, Dengue IgM/IgG, Platelet count

diseases.name: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Prolonged PT/PTT with thrombocytopenia and elevated D-dimer in a critically ill patient'

diseases.name: Aplastic Anemia
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests names Platelet Count as one of the three lines assessed

cohorts.name: Thrombocytosis
cohorts.description: Platelet count above range. Most cases are reactive to iron deficiency, inflammation or infection.

supporting.label: Low ferritin - iron deficiency is the commonest reactive cause

evidence.citation: Bleeker JS, Hogan WJ, Thrombosis 2011;2011:536062
evidence.note: Reactive thrombocytosis accounts for the large majority of raised platelet counts; iron deficiency and inflammation are the leading causes.

diseases.name: Thrombocytosis (Reactive/Secondary)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Persistently elevated platelet count without an obvious reactive cause'; Related Markers/Tests: Platelet count (from CBC/Blood Counts panel)

diseases.name: Iron Deficiency Anemia
diseases.dm_basis: Cross-linked because iron deficiency is the commonest identifiable reactive trigger; confirmed by the ferritin result

cohorts.name: Prolonged Prothrombin Time / INR
cohorts.description: Prolongation of the extrinsic pathway. Causes divide into vitamin K deficiency, liver disease and anticoagulant effect - distinguished by the accompanying results.

supporting.label: INR at or above 3.5 - bleeding risk range
Albumin low - points toward hepatic rather than vitamin K cause
APTT also prolonged - both pathways affected
Thrombocytopenia - raises the possibility of consumption

evidence.citation: Tripodi A, Mannucci PM, N Engl J Med 2011;365:147-56
evidence.note: Interpretation of prolonged PT/INR in liver disease versus vitamin K deficiency.

evidence.citation: Keeling D et al., BCSH Guidelines on Oral Anticoagulation with Warfarin, Br J Haematol 2011;154:311-24
evidence.note: Therapeutic INR ranges and the bleeding risk associated with supratherapeutic values.

diseases.name: Vitamin K Deficiency
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Prolonged PT/INR responsive to vitamin K supplementation'; Related Markers/Tests: PT (Prothrombin Time), PT-INR

diseases.name: Liver-related Coagulopathy
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Prolonged PT/INR with abnormal LFTs (low albumin, elevated bilirubin/transaminases)'

diseases.name: Anticoagulant Therapy Monitoring
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'INR outside the prescribed therapeutic range (too high = bleeding risk, too low = clotting risk)'; Classification 'Other' - a monitoring context, not a disease

diseases.name: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Prolonged PT/PTT with thrombocytopenia and elevated D-dimer'

cohorts.name: Isolated APTT Prolongation
cohorts.description: APTT prolonged while the prothrombin time stays normal - the screening pattern for an intrinsic pathway factor deficiency.

supporting.label: INR normal - the prolongation is confined to the intrinsic pathway
Prothrombin time normal - confirms an isolated APTT prolongation
Platelet count normal - argues against a consumptive process

evidence.citation: Srivastava A et al., WFH Guidelines for the Management of Hemophilia, 3rd edition, Haemophilia 2020;26(S6):1-158
evidence.note: Prolonged APTT with normal PT as the screening pattern for haemophilia A/B, requiring factor assays for confirmation.

evidence.citation: James PD et al., ASH/ISTH/NHF/WFH 2021 Guidelines on the Diagnosis of von Willebrand Disease, Blood Adv 2021;5:280-300
evidence.note: APTT may be normal or only mildly prolonged in von Willebrand disease; bleeding history drives testing.

diseases.name: Hemophilia (A/B)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Prolonged APTT with normal PT, especially with a personal/family history of unusual bleeding or joint bleeds'; Related Markers/Tests: Prothrombin Time/APTT

diseases.name: Von Willebrand Disease
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests: 'Prothrombin Time/APTT (often normal or mildly prolonged APTT)'; High-Risk Indicators rest on the bleeding history

cohorts.name: Consumptive Coagulopathy Pattern
cohorts.description: Simultaneous prolongation of both pathways, falling platelets and raised D-dimer - the laboratory signature of disseminated intravascular coagulation.

supporting.label: CRP raised - infection or inflammation as a trigger

evidence.citation: Taylor FB et al., ISTH Scoring System for Overt DIC, Thromb Haemost 2001;86:1327-30
evidence.note: The ISTH DIC score combines platelet count, fibrin marker (D-dimer), prolonged PT and fibrinogen - the components implemented here.

evidence.citation: Levi M, Sivapalaratnam S, Expert Rev Hematol 2018;11:663-72
evidence.note: Laboratory diagnosis of DIC as a composite rather than a single test.

diseases.name: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Prolonged PT/PTT with thrombocytopenia and elevated D-dimer in a critically ill patient'; Related Markers/Tests: PT, PT-INR, PTT

diseases.name: Sepsis
diseases.dm_basis: External Risk Factors and Possible Complications on the Sepsis row identify DIC as a recognised complication of severe sepsis

cohorts.name: Raised Fibrin Degradation Signal
cohorts.description: D-dimer above the exclusion threshold. Useful for ruling thromboembolism out; on its own it does not rule it in.

supporting.label: CRP raised - inflammation also raises D-dimer

evidence.citation: Wells PS et al., N Engl J Med 2003;349:1227-35
evidence.note: D-dimer combined with clinical probability to exclude deep vein thrombosis; a raised result is non-specific.

evidence.citation: Konstantinides SV et al., 2019 ESC Guidelines on Acute Pulmonary Embolism, Eur Heart J 2020;41:543-603
evidence.note: D-dimer has high sensitivity and low specificity; imaging is required to confirm.

diseases.name: Venous Thromboembolism (VTE)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated D-Dimer with clinical signs of DVT/PE'; Related Markers/Tests: D-Dimer, PT TEST. Weight held at moderate because the Disease Master indicator requires clinical signs the lab data cannot supply.

diseases.name: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators include 'elevated D-dimer' as one of four components

cohorts.name: Haemolysis Pattern
cohorts.description: Anaemia with raised unconjugated bilirubin, raised LDH and a reticulocyte response - indicating red cell destruction rather than underproduction.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: Haemolysis can only be recognised by combining Blood Counts (haemoglobin, reticulocytes) with Liver Profile (indirect bilirubin) and LDH. No single profile carries the pattern.

triggers.label: Reticulocyte count raised - marrow response to red cell loss

evidence.citation: Barcellini W, Fattizzo B, Dis Markers 2015;2015:635670
evidence.note: Raised LDH and unconjugated bilirubin with reticulocytosis and low haptoglobin as the standard haemolysis marker set.

evidence.citation: Luzzatto L, Ally M, Notaro R, Blood 2020;136:1225-40
evidence.note: G6PD deficiency: episodic haemolysis triggered by oxidative stress.

diseases.name: G6PD Deficiency
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low quantitative G6PD enzyme level'; Severity/Urgency: 'urgent during acute hemolytic episode'

diseases.name: Sickle Cell Disease
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive sickling test confirmed on electrophoresis'

diseases.name: Thalassemia (Trait/Major)
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests: Hemoglobin, RBC indices, Hemoglobin electrophoresis - ineffective erythropoiesis produces a similar biochemical picture

cohorts.name: G6PD Enzyme Deficiency
cohorts.description: Low quantitative G6PD activity, which predisposes to oxidative haemolysis after specific drug, food or infection triggers.

triggers.label: Quantitative G6PD enzyme activity below range

evidence.citation: Luzzatto L, Ally M, Notaro R, Blood 2020;136:1225-40
evidence.note: Quantitative enzyme assay as the diagnostic test; results can be falsely normal during an acute haemolytic episode.

diseases.name: G6PD Deficiency
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low quantitative G6PD enzyme level'; Related Markers/Tests: G6PD (Quantitative)

cohorts.name: Abnormal Haemoglobin Fraction
cohorts.description: A structurally abnormal haemoglobin or an abnormal fraction on electrophoresis.

evidence.citation: Kato GJ et al., Nat Rev Dis Primers 2018;4:18010
evidence.note: Sickle cell disease: solubility screening confirmed by electrophoresis or HPLC.

evidence.citation: Ryan K et al., BCSH Significant Haemoglobinopathies Guideline, Br J Haematol 2010;149:35-49
evidence.note: HbA2 and HbF quantitation in the laboratory diagnosis of haemoglobinopathies.

diseases.name: Sickle Cell Disease
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Positive sickling test confirmed on electrophoresis'; Related Markers/Tests: Sickle Cell Solubility Test, Hemoglobin Electrophoresis

diseases.name: Thalassemia (Trait/Major)
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests: Hemoglobin, RBC indices, Hemoglobin electrophoresis

diseases.name: Hemoglobin C/E Disease (HbC/HbE)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Mild microcytic anemia with an abnormal hemoglobin fraction on electrophoresis not explained by iron deficiency or thalassemia alone'

cohorts.name: Monoclonal Gammopathy (CRAB) Pattern
cohorts.description: Raised total protein and globulin with hypercalcaemia, renal impairment or anaemia - the CRAB features named in the clinical reference.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: The CRAB acronym is inherently cross-profile: Calcium from Electrolyte Profile, Renal from Kidney Profile, Anaemia from Blood Counts, and the paraprotein signal from Total Protein/Globulin in the Liver Profile.

supporting.label: ESR markedly raised - typical of a paraproteinaemia
RDW-SD raised (noted in the Disease Master as prognostic in known cases, not a screening marker)

evidence.citation: Rajkumar SV et al., International Myeloma Working Group updated criteria, Lancet Oncol 2014;15:e538-48
evidence.note: CRAB criteria (hyperCalcaemia, Renal insufficiency, Anaemia, Bone lesions) define myeloma requiring therapy.

evidence.citation: Kyle RA, Rajkumar SV, N Engl J Med 2004;351:1860-73
evidence.note: Serum protein abnormalities as the initial laboratory clue to monoclonal gammopathy.

diseases.name: Multiple Myeloma
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated total protein/globulin with hypercalcemia, anemia, or unexplained bone pain - the classic CRAB pattern (Calcium, Renal, Anemia, Bone)'; Related Markers/Tests: Total Protein, Globulin, Calcium, RDW-SD

diseases.name: Hyperparathyroidism
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated calcium with elevated PTH, especially with low phosphorus' - the main alternative explanation for hypercalcaemia

cohorts.name: Rh-Negative Blood Group
cohorts.description: Rh-negative status, relevant to pregnancy planning because of the risk of alloimmunisation against an Rh-positive fetus.

evidence.citation: Qureshi H et al., BCSH Guideline for the Use of Anti-D Immunoglobulin, Transfus Med 2014;24:8-20
evidence.note: Rh-negative status in pregnancy and the role of anti-D prophylaxis in preventing haemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn.

diseases.name: Rh Incompatibility/Hemolytic Disease of the Newborn
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Rh-negative mother carrying an Rh-positive fetus, especially with a positive antibody screen'; Related Markers/Tests: Blood Group, Rh Factor. Weight held at moderate because pregnancy status and fetal Rh type are not lab-derivable.
